findings.title: Crash when Google Meet is selected and no destination calendar exists
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendars (e.g. `handleNewBooking` now sets `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one). The next line then dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`, throwing a TypeError. This is exactly the code path the check was written for (Google Meet selected without a Google Calendar), so instead of falling back to Cal Video the whole booking request now fails with a 500. Needs optional access (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`).

findings.title: Video booking references lose credentialId, breaking meeting deletion/updates
findings.body: In `create()`, `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` replaces the previous `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. For non-calendar (video) results the credentialId is now always `undefined`, so `BookingReference` rows of type `*_video` are persisted without a credentialId. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set (`if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`), and seat cancellation/update paths also key off `reference.credentialId`. Result: video meetings created after this change are never cancelled or updated on the provider.

findings.title: updateLocation writes references with an always-undefined externalCalendarId
findings.body: `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` is used for the references created by `updateLocation()`, but `updateEvent()` in `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` never sets `externalId` on its returned `EventResult` (only `createEvent` does). So `result.externalId` is always `undefined` here and the new `BookingReference` rows lose the external calendar id that was previously taken from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Later cancel/reschedule flows that rely on `reference.externalCalendarId` will then fall back to the provider's primary calendar and fail to find the event.

findings.title: Destination calendars without credentialId lose their externalId in references and events
findings.body: In `createAllCalendarEvents`, the branch for a destination without `credentialId` calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`. Because `EventResult.externalId` is what now populates `referencesToCreate.externalCalendarId` (see line 169), those bookings get references with no external calendar id. Combined with the Google service now resolving the target calendar by `credentialId` match only, such events are also created in `"primary"` instead of the configured destination calendar. Previously `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId` was used for both the reference and the target calendar.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents failures are now silently swallowed
findings.body: The `console.error(message)` call was removed from the catch block, but `message` is still built from the error. Any failure while updating calendar events (including an `undefined` credential being passed to `updateEvent`) now returns fake failed results with no log line at all, making production diagnosis of calendar update failures impossible.

findings.title: updateEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — the `find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId === undefined` and always returns `undefined`. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Consequently `calendar.events.update({ calendarId: undefined })` is issued whenever no external calendar id is stored on the booking reference, so updates/reschedules of events living in a non-primary destination calendar fail.

findings.title: deleteEvent always falls back to 'primary' calendar
findings.body: Same dead-condition as in `updateEvent`: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always yields `undefined` and `calendarId` becomes `defaultCalendarId` (`"primary"`). Previously the destination calendar's `externalId` was used. Cancellations for bookings stored in a non-primary Google calendar will now hit the primary calendar, return 404 (swallowed as success) and leave the real event in place.

findings.title: events.patch is called with a possibly undefined calendarId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` can now be `undefined` (the `|| "primary"` default was only applied inline at the `events.insert` call). The follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` that writes the hangout link into the description still uses the raw value, producing a malformed request URL when no destination calendar matches the credential. The promise is not awaited or caught, so this fails silently and the Meet link is missing from the event description.

findings.title: createEvent target calendar now resolved only by credentialId match
findings.body: `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` replaces the former `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable, and `EventManager` reaches this service via the no-credentialId branch for such rows (passing no credential match), so for every destination calendar with a null `credentialId` the event is now created in `"primary"` instead of the user-selected calendar — a silent regression for existing single-host setups.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent reports success while creating nothing for secondary hosts
findings.body: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates every destination calendar and calls `createEvent` with that host's credential, but this service still filters the account's calendars against `destinationCalendar[0]` (the main host). When invoked with a second host's credential, no calendar URL matches, `responses` is an empty array, `responses.some((r) => !r.ok)` is false, and the method returns a success result with a fresh uid even though no event was created on any calendar. The booking reference is stored and the host never gets the event, with no error surfaced.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first host's calendar id
findings.body: Only `destinationCalendar[0]` is honoured. With the new multi-destination flow, `EventManager` calls `createEvent` once per destination using that destination's owner credential; for the second host this builds `/me/calendars/<first host's calendar id>/events` while authenticating as the second host, which 404s (or writes to the wrong calendar if ids happen to collide). The service should select the destination matching the credential it was constructed with (as the Google service now does via the new `credentialId` argument).

findings.title: Lark createEvent/createAttendees always use the first host's calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` is used for the calendar id in `createEvent`, `createAttendees`, `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`. Since `EventManager` now invokes these once per destination calendar with the corresponding host's credential, every host's run targets the first host's calendar id, producing duplicate events on the main host's calendar (or API errors) and no event on the other hosts' calendars.

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when no primary destination exists
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining, but `destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. In that case the collected co-host destination calendars are silently discarded and the very bug this PR targets (collective hosts not getting calendar events) remains for teams whose organizer has no destination calendar. Initialise the array (e.g. `[]`) before pushing.

findings.title: organization relation dropped from the dynamic-booking user select
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` removes `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the `prisma.user.findMany` select used for dynamic (no eventTypeId) bookings, while the host-based branch keeps whatever the event type query selected. Any downstream use of `user.organization` for dynamic group bookings now sees `undefined` (and the two branches no longer return the same shape, so the inferred union type changes). This change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar fix and should be reverted unless the field is provably unused.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes every event once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring/`allRemainingBookings` block, which already loops over all of the user's calendar credentials and all updated bookings, is now nested inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references the same delete calls are issued N times (N × credentials × bookings), multiplying provider API calls and rate-limit risk; the outer `calendar` instance created from `calendarCredential` is also unused in that branch. The recurring branch should run once, outside the per-reference loop.

findings.title: Organization slug assignment logic inverted
findings.body: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was changed to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This inverts the intent: with team billing enabled the slug is now set immediately *and* duplicated into `metadata.requestedSlug` (the slug is supposed to be claimed only after payment), while with billing disabled the organization is created with no slug at all, leaving it unreachable by its subdomain. This change is also unrelated to the destinationCalendar fix in this PR.

findings.title: Webhook/CalendarEvent payload shape changed from object to array without versioning
findings.body: `destinationCalendar` changes from `DestinationCalendar | null` to `DestinationCalendar[] | null`. This field is forwarded verbatim to webhook subscribers via `sendPayload` (see the e2e expectations, which now mix `destinationCalendar: null` for BOOKING_CREATED/REQUESTED and `[]` for BOOKING_REJECTED). External consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will break, and the payload is now inconsistent (`null` vs `[]` vs array) depending on the code path. The shape should be normalised and the breaking payload change documented.

findings.title: No tests for the new multi-destination calendar fan-out
findings.body: `createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` now loop over an array of destination calendars, fetch foreign credentials from the DB and build one reference per created event, and every provider service was touched. The only test change in the PR is flipping one e2e expectation from `null` to `[]`. There is no unit/integration coverage asserting that a collective event with two hosts creates exactly one event per host calendar, that references carry the right `credentialId`/`externalCalendarId`, or that the single-host fallback is unchanged — all of which the findings above show are currently broken for several providers.
